title: Core of the Truehearted 1
content:
The Bloodbath of the Nightless City: legend held that the Yiling Patriarch, Wei Wuxian, had single-handedly slaughtered all three thousand cultivators gathered for the pledge assembly that night.

Some rumors claimed the body count was well over five thousand. But whether it was three thousand or five thousand, one thing remained indisputable: on that horrific night, Wei Wuxian turned the ruins of the Nightless City into a gore-drenched living hell.

Yet even with thousands baying for his blood, the murderer had somehow managed to walk away completely unscathed, slipping right back to the Burial Mounds. To this day, nobody knew how he pulled it off.

The prominent sects took a devastating blow in that battle. It took nearly three solid months of licking their wounds and drafting battle strategies before the Four Great Clans finally rallied together to launch their crusade against the demonic den of the Burial Mounds. They returned the word "slaughter" in kind—wiping out the remaining Wen Clan survivors and taking down the crazed Yiling Patriarch.

Wei Wuxian took a long look at the cultivators massed in front of the Demon-Subduing Cave. The hatred etched across their faces was a mirror image of the men who had poured libations on the flagstones that night, screaming their blood oaths to grind his bones to dust. Some in the crowd were actual survivors from that battle; others were sons and daughters taking up fallen blades; but the vast majority were self-proclaimed "paragons of justice," fueled by that very same righteous frenzy.

The middle-aged cultivator who claimed Wei Wuxian had hacked off his leg—forcing him to limp on a wooden peg—stepped forward. Yi Weichun snarled, "Three thousand dead souls! You couldn't balance that ledger if you died ten thousand deaths!"

Wei Wuxian cut him off cleanly. "Three thousand? Sure, three thousand-odd cultivators showed up that night. But the grand leaders of the great clans were standing right there, flanked by their most elite disciples and senior masters. With titans like that on the field, you honestly believe I could wipe out three thousand people down to the last man? Are you giving me too much credit, or do you just think your own leaders are completely useless?"

He was merely laying out the facts, yet the man took it as a personal, venomous slight. Yi Weichun barked, "What the hell do you think this is, a business transaction?! You think you can haggle over a blood debt?!"

"I'm not haggling," Wei Wuxian said evenly. "I just don't feel like letting people double my body count based on wild gossip. If I didn't do it, I'm not taking the fall for it."

Someone jeered from the crowd, "Didn't do it? What haven't you done?!"

Wei Wuxian counted them off: "For starters, I wasn't the one who had Chifeng-zun quartered by five horses. I didn't drive Madame Jin to commit suicide on Koi Tower. And these walking corpses you spent the entire hike hacking through? Hate to break it to you, but I wasn't the one pulling their strings either."

Su She sneered, his lips curling with mocking derision. "Yiling Patriarch, everyone knows you're arrogant, but I never pegged you for a modest man. If it wasn't you, I can't imagine who else in the world could herd this many fierce corpses, running us ragged up the mountain."

"What's so hard to imagine?" Wei Wuxian countered smoothly. "Hand anyone the Yin Tiger Tally, and they could pull off the exact same circus."

Su She narrowed his eyes. "And isn't that tally your personal spiritual weapon?"

"That depends on who has been drooling over it in secret, doesn't it?" Wei Wuxian drawled. "Take Wen Ning, for instance. Certain prominent clans were scared to death of the Ghost General, screaming bloody murder about putting him down, while secretly locking him in a basement for over a decade. Funny, wasn't someone swearing up and down back then that they'd already ground his bones into ash?"

Unconsciously, countless eyes darted toward the Lanling Jin contingent. After all, the man who had taken full charge of the executions, swore he had reduced the two Wen ringleaders to cinder, and dramatically scattered their ashes across the Nightless City had been none other than the sect leader of Lanling Jin.

Caught out, Su She snapped, "Stop trying to stir up trouble!"

Right then, a frantic rustle and a chorus of guttural, rattling wheezes drifted from the dark timber.

Lan Qiren’s voice boomed with urgent authority: "Everyone on guard! A fresh wave of fierce corpses is inbound!"

Half the crowd whipped around to meet the threat, while the other half kept their blades leveled squarely at the "rabble" before the cave mouth.

Wei Wuxian sighed. "Like I said, I'm not holding the leash on these things. If you've got time to stare at me, you'd better start looking at them."

The field was packed with seasoned veterans, clan leaders, and venerable elders; taking down a wave of dead flesh was usually child's play. In an instant, sword-glare flashed and zither notes pierced the air, leaving no one with the luxury to babysit Wei Wuxian. Jiang Cheng swung his whip, pulverizing three charging corpses to dust, then wheeled around to roar at Jin Ling: "Jin Ling! Do you want to keep your damn legs or not?!"

It was his signature threat—promising to snap the boy's legs if he didn't fall into line. But Jin Ling had heard that line a thousand times without it ever being carried out, so he merely cut Jiang Cheng a sullen side-eye and stayed put. Jiang Cheng let out a foul curse. Snapping his wrist, he coiled Zidian, intending to lash out and drag the brat back by force.

Then, without warning, the vibrant purple lightning dancing along the whip crackled, dimmed, and sputtered out like a dying candle.

The crackling lash instantly collapsed back into a simple silver ring around his index finger. Jiang Cheng froze, staring at his bare hand in absolute disbelief. Zidian had never retracted on its own before. As he turned his palm over, two warm crimson drops splattered onto his skin.

He wiped his nose with the back of his hand, coming away with a smear of fresh, wet blood.

Jin Ling’s voice cracked in horror: "Jiujiu!"

All across the battlefield, cries of sheer panic erupted in frantic waves. Looking across the clearing, the brilliant spiritual glare on eight or nine out of ten swords had flickered out into dead iron. Nearly half the cultivators stood in a daze, twin trails of dark red bleeding steadily from their noses. Others were spitting mouthfuls of crimson, blood pouring freely from their lips and nostrils!

A swordsman stumbled, his voice shaking: "What's happening?!"

"My spiritual energy... it's gone!"

"Shixiong, help me! Something's wrong with my core!"

Bichen unsheathed with a pristine chime, bisecting two corpses that were lunging at a shrieking disciple. But the frantic pleas for help multiplied by the second, overlapping in a rising tide of panic as the crowd broke ranks, stumbling backward toward the mouth of the Demon-Subduing Cave.

The righteous warriors who had marched up the Burial Mounds ready to paint the peak in blood had all lost their spiritual cores in a single, inexplicable breath. The glows of their swords died, their talismans were reduced to useless scraps of paper, and the spiritual melodies of the Lan and Su disciples decayed into ordinary, hollow tunes that couldn't repel a single ghost.

The board had completely flipped!

Lan Wangji unslung his guqin, fingers tearing across the seven strings to unleash deafening sonic booms. Yet no matter how peerless his chord techniques were, he was still just one man holding the line. Wen Ning vaulted down the stone steps of the cave, tossing corpses aside with raw, concussive brute force, stoically taking a storm of accidental slashes, stabs, and kicks from the terrified cultivators in the process. Fortunately, dead flesh felt no pain, and he didn't flinch.

Amidst the stampede and blind hysteria, Lan Sizhui suddenly bolted to the threshold, yelling at the top of his lungs: "Everyone, fall back! Get inside the Demon-Subduing Cave! There's a massive warding array carved into the floor—it's missing a few runes, but if we patch it up, it'll hold them off for a while!"

A few cultivators on the brink of being torn to shreds moved to rush the doors, but Su She shouted them down: "Don't go in! It's a trap—they want us cornered like rats in a barrel! There's bound to be a fatal ambush waiting for us inside!"

The crowd hesitated, frozen in paralyzing dread. Wei Wuxian flicked his wrists, tossing out sixty-odd scattering talismans in a blinding blaze of fire. "Die out here, die in there—you're dead meat either way! Getting inside buys us time. What's your rush to drag everyone to an early grave, Sect Leader Su?"

It was sound logic, but because the advice came from the Yiling Patriarch himself, the mob only became more paranoid, desperately throwing their bare hands against the advancing dead. The seasoned fighters could hold their own for a few minutes on pure martial grit, but Nie Huaisang wasn't having any of it. Everyone knew he was a hopeless slacker with zero talent and a cowardly streak a mile wide; cornered by the sudden disaster, he was practically flapping his arms in blind panic, barely surviving thanks to a few bodyguards throwing their lives on the line. Seeing the endless black tide of corpses spilling from the woods, he waved frantically: "Are you guys getting in or not?! If you're staying out, I'm heading in! Excuse me, coming through—everyone get your asses inside!"

Before he even finished speaking, Nie Huaisang took off like a rabbit, leading the entire Qinghe Nie contingent barreling into the cave like dogs running for shelter.

The crowd stood slack-jawed at his shameless honesty.

Right then, Ouyang Zizhen shouted, "Father, stop fighting! Trust me, get inside! We literally just walked out of that cave—there are no traps in there!"

The other youths chimed in: "He's right! There really is a massive array carved on the floor!"

Jin Ling yelled down at his uncle. "Jiujiu, get in!"

Jiang Cheng swung Sandu's dull blade with raw muscle, barking, "Shut your damn mouth!"

The roar pulled another fresh spurt of blood from his nose and lips. Jin Ling bolted down the steps, grabbed Jiang Cheng by the collar, and physically dragged him toward the threshold. His spiritual power gone and having spent half the day fighting for his life, Jiang Cheng was utterly drained—leaving him completely powerless to resist as his nephew hauled him inside, with the remaining Jiang disciples scrambling in behind them.

From deep within the cavern, Nie Huaisang’s panicked, echoing voice drifted out: "Everyone hurry up and get in! It's huge in here! Can one of you seniors come patch up this array on the floor?! I don't know how! I have no idea what runes to draw!"

Hearing that final whine, a single collective thought crossed every mind on the field: Useless trash!

Lan Wangji kept his hands on the strings, calling out, "Uncle!"

Lan Qiren hadn't wanted to retreat; he would have preferred to fight to his last breath out in the open. But he wasn't standing alone—he had a sea of young Lan disciples and the Jin forces entrusted to his command behind him. He couldn't gamble with their lives; if there was a sliver of survival, he had to take it. Refusing to meet Lan Wangji's eyes, he raised his blade and barked: "Move inside! Stay on your guard!"

With that, all Four Great Clans—Lanling Jin, Gusu Lan, Qinghe Nie, and Yunmeng Jiang—had crossed the threshold. With the heavyweights leading the charge, the rest of the mob abandoned their pride, swarming inside like floodwaters. Even if there were monsters waiting in the dark, the four giants would take the brunt of the hit.

In the end, only the Moling Su Sect was left standing in the dirt.

Wei Wuxian tilted his head. "My, my, Sect Leader Su, not coming in? Suit yourself, feel free to enjoy the breeze out here. Though since everyone's cores are shot, staying outside is basically suicide, isn't it? Truly admirable courage."

Su She glared daggers, a muscle in his jaw twitching violently as he shoved his way inside with his disciples close behind.

The cavern swallowed the thousand-strong crowd with room to spare. The chamber filled with ragged panting, frantic murmurs, and suffocating dread echoing off the damp rock walls. Lan Qiren marched straight over to Nie Huaisang, inspecting the fractured ward under the man’s desperate, pleading stare. The array was ancient; slicing his own palm, Lan Qiren used fresh blood to bridge the missing strokes. Outside on the steps, Wen Ning hurled the nearest charging corpses away with concussive force. The moment the final rune was restored, an invisible barrier snapped into place, locking the dead on the other side of the threshold.

Wei Wuxian waited until Lan Wangji stowed his instrument before strolling inside together. The second the crowd spotted the twin silhouettes descending the stone steps—one draped in ink, the other in snow—a thousand hearts leaped right into their throats.

Nobody could have predicted this absolute farce. They had marched up the mountain to exterminate the Yiling Patriarch, only to get hunted like sheep and forced to beg for shelter inside the demon's very living room.

Having finished patching the array, Lan Qiren planted himself squarely in front of the crowd, blocking their path with an iron posture—looking for all the world like he was prepared to trade his ancient life to drag Wei Wuxian to hell if the youth so much as looked at the ward funny.

Lan Wangji murmured softly, "...Uncle."

The deep, stinging disappointment hadn't faded; Lan Qiren couldn't bring himself to look at his prized pupil. He fixed a frosty stare on Wei Wuxian instead. "What is your game?"

Wei Wuxian casually dropped down onto a stone step. "No game. Since we're all packed in here, why not have a chat..."

Yi Weichun spat, "We have nothing to say to you!"

"Nothing to say?" Wei Wuxian chuckled. "Don't tell me you aren't dying to know why your spiritual energy vanished into thin air? Cross my heart, I don't have the godlike ability to knock out a thousand golden cores without a single person noticing."

Yi Weichun sneered, but Nie Huaisang chimed in from the back: "You know... he kind of has a point."

A sea of furious glares whipped around to burn holes through him.

Wei Wuxian carried on: "I'm guessing you lot didn't sit down for a massive banquet together before storming up the hill, so we can rule out poison in the food."

Lan Sizhui offered, "It can't be poison. I've never heard of a toxin that instantly scatters spiritual energy across hundreds of cultivators. If such a concoction existed, sects would be butchering each other to buy it for astronomical sums."

Several clan physicians were among the ranks, frantically checking pulses. Cultivators leaned in, whispering in frantic terror: "How is it?! Is the dispersion temporary or permanent?!"

The dread in that single question made everyone forget about Wei Wuxian entirely. Losing your golden core forever meant being reduced to an ordinary, crippled mortal—a fate infinitely more agonizing than getting torn apart by corpses. After a frantic huddle, the healers finally exhaled: "Your cores are intact and unblemished! Rest easy, it should be temporary!"

Hearing that, Jiang Cheng quietly let out a breath he didn't realize he'd been holding. Taking a handkerchief from Jin Ling, he wiped the crusted blood from his face and demanded: "Temporary? How long is temporary? When does it come back?"

A physician hesitated, sweating: "...I fear... at least four hours..."

Jiang Cheng’s expression turned murderous. "Four hours?!"

Heads turned toward the cave entrance. Outside the shimmering barrier, the walking dead had formed an iron ring, easily matching the headcount of the living trapped inside. Hundreds of milky, pupilless eyes were fixed on the warm, living bodies packed in the hall, refusing to budge an inch, jostling against the unseen ward in an endless sea of rotting flesh and sickening stench.

Four hours? A makeshift, ancient array patched up with a palmful of blood—who knew if it could even hold for four minutes!

Worse, the Yiling Patriarch was locked in the room with them. Sure, he hadn't struck yet, but who was to say he wasn't just playing cat-and-mouse, waiting to toy with them until they were paralyzed with terror before crushing them under his heel?

Eyes snapped back to Wei Wuxian.

He waved a dismissive hand. "Told you, stop staring at me. Right now, there are only two groups in this cave who still have their spiritual power: Hanguang-jun and myself, and these kids who were dragged up the mountain days ago. As for the rest of you, calling you defenseless isn't an exaggeration, is it? If I actually wanted to do something to you, you think these teenagers could stop me?"

Su She sneered, "Save your breath. If you're going to butcher us, do it now. Not a single man here will scream for mercy, and you can forget about seeing anyone beg on their knees."

That little speech pulled uneasy frowns from quite a few faces. Out of the thousands packed in the cavern, barely twenty had any genuine, personal vendetta against Wei Wuxian. The rest were just jumping on the righteous bandwagon—following the herd to bask in the glory of hunting the great evil, hoping to bag a few corpses to brag about back home. But if staying meant paying with their actual lives, almost nobody wanted to drown in this muddy water.

Wei Wuxian squinted at him. "Excuse me, but... who the hell are you?"

A thick vein throbbed on Su She’s forehead. Just as he opened his mouth to snap, Lan Jingyi barked: "And then what?! It's not poison, so what is it?!"

Wei Wuxian forgot about Su She in an instant. "Then, people don't just lose their cores out of thin air; there has to be a vector and a trigger. You must have all touched the same thing, or done the exact same action on the way up. The kids were kidnapped days ago, so their timing was different; Hanguang-jun and I took a separate trail, so our path was different. Does anyone want to use their brain and think about what you all did?"

In the heavy silence, a baffled voice piped up: "What did we do? Did we all drink the water on the way up? Ah, I can't remember, I have no idea."

Who else would be tone-deaf enough to eagerly brainstorm with the Yiling Patriarch right now? None other than the resident "Master of Cluelessness," Nie Huaisang.

Someone snapped, "Nobody touched the water on that path! Who would be crazy enough to drink from a mountain of corpses?!"

Nie Huaisang guessed again, "Did we breathe in the mist in the woods?"

If the dark fog carried some foul miasma, it made sense. A few murmured in agreement, but Jin Ling cut them down immediately: "Impossible. The mist is twice as thick at the summit, and we've been tied up on that peak for two days straight—our spiritual energy is completely fine!"

Su She couldn't stomach another second. "Are you serious?! You're actually sitting here brainstorming with the enemy? Getting led by the nose by the villain—is this amusing to you? He—"

Suddenly, his face seized, his voice choking off in his throat.

Wei Wuxian smiled. "Go on. What happened to the speech?"

The Moling Su disciples scrambled to their feet: "Sect Leader!" "Sect Leader, what's wrong?!"

Su She violently shoved his disciples aside, his arm trembling as he pointed a furious finger at Wei Wuxian, before snapping it straight toward Lan Wangji.

A nearby disciple barked, "Wei Wuxian! What foul sorcery did you just pull?!"

Lan Sizhui blurted out, "That's not sorcery! That's... that's..."

Seated in pure stillness, Lan Wangji brought the five fingers of his right hand flat against the seven strings of his guqin, stilling the final vibration of the notes.

The clamoring disciples were silenced on the spot, like a flock of squawking ducks caught by the neck.

Every Lan cultivator in the room shared the exact same thought in dead silence: ...That's the Gusu Lan Clan's Silence Spell.
